title: The Human Reference Genome: GRCh38 (hg38)
description: The Human reference genome (Homo sapiens, assembly GRCh38 (hg38)) spans approximately 3.05 Gb across 24 (22 autosomes + X, Y) chromosomes, encoding approx 20,000 protein-coding genes (GENCODE; estimate). This record is the assembly-level overview: the anchor for the deterministic scale chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait used across this database. REFERENCE GENOME ONLY: a public consensus assembly, never any real person's private genetic data.
how_it_works: Genome assembly stitches long sequencing reads into chromosome-scale scaffolds, annotates genes by homology and experiment, and publishes the consensus coordinates everyone references. All records in this database hang off these coordinates deterministically.
key_points: Assembly GRCh38 (hg38): the public reference coordinates.
Size approximately 3.05 Gb; 24 (22 autosomes + X, Y).
Gene content: approx 20,000 protein-coding genes (GENCODE; estimate).
standards: Coordinates follow the named assembly GRCh38 (hg38)
Numeric values are approximate unless stated; estimates are labeled

demo.note: Prints the deterministic scale ladder for this genome.

provenance: JAH Databases genome lane (r18); public reference assembly facts; nucleotide examples are synthetic representative motifs, never real reference sequence and never any individual genome.

title: Human Chromosome 1 (GRCh38 (hg38))
description: Chromosome 1 of the Human reference genome (assembly GRCh38 (hg38)). Each chromosome is a deterministic address space: genes live at fixed coordinates on it, so gene -> protein -> pathway -> trait records resolve unambiguously. Sizes here are approximate (labeled estimates).
how_it_works: Chromosomes package DNA with histones into chromatin; genes are transcribed from fixed loci. The demo computes this chromosome's approximate share of the whole genome.

title: Human: The Deterministic Scale Ladder
description: The Deterministic Scale Ladder (Human). chromosome -> gene -> protein product -> pathway -> trait: each level is a deterministic function of the level below in the reference assembly. No level is a sample or a guess; the ladder is the database's spine.
how_it_works: Scaling walks the ladder deterministically: pick a level, apply its rules, land on the next level. The generator ladder ranks are simple -> most competitive -> mix-and-match -> unmade -> top-notch -> future grade -> god mode.
key_points: Deterministic: same level, same rules, same result.
Generator bound: stops at 10^15 records or complete-with-reason.
standards: Scaling claims are structural, not empirical, and labeled as such
